summary: Round r1 (restricted network). All empirical items pending; no document downloaded. Leads identified for Q1 (ICIMOD Glacier Outlook 2026 benchmark mass-balance series, ICIMOD Nepal glacier inventory 1980-2010 and HKH 1990-2020 change, HKH Assessment Ch.7, HI-WISE 2023, IPCC SROCC Ch.2 and AR6 WGI Ch.9), Q2 (DNPWC and WDPA for protected areas; FRTC national forest assessment, FAO FRA 2020 and WDI for forest cover; Global Forest Watch as a separate satellite tree-cover indicator) and Q3 (Khadka 2020 Koshi, Lutz 2014, Huss and Hock 2018, HI-WISE, WECS basin plans, DHM observed discharge). 13B relies on 25A for projection ranges and does not duplicate them. Key methodological issues: in-situ vs geodetic mass balance; forest land-use vs tree-cover definitions; protected area with vs without buffer zones; glacier-runoff vs total-runoff; CMIP5 vs CMIP6 scenario framing. Glacier mass balance lacks a unit code in units.py.

findings.claim: Q1: Documented glacier mass-balance trend for Nepal basins (in-situ benchmark glaciers and geodetic regional estimates), with period and method.
findings.period: hydrological years (calendar-based, glacier-specific); multi-decade geodetic periods
findings.note: Required: benchmark glacier annual mass-balance series (ICIMOD Glacier Outlook 2026); geodetic mass balance for Central/Eastern Himalaya (HKH Ch.7, HI-WISE, AR6 WGI Ch.9); inventory area change by basin (ICIMOD 2014, 1990-2020 study). Unit metre water-equivalent per year has no code in units.py; see challenge to 00A.

findings.claim: Q2a: Protected-area coverage of Nepal's territory (national parks, reserves, conservation areas, buffer zones), with reference date.
findings.period: as of gazettement date / WDPA vintage (calendar)
findings.note: Required: DNPWC area list; WDPA extract; WDI ER.PTD.TOTL.ZS. Keep with/without buffer zones distinct.

findings.period: FRA reference years (calendar) and national assessment years (Nepal FY/BS)
findings.note: Required: FRTC national assessment and local-level maps; FAO FRA 2020 series; GFW tree-cover loss as separate satellite indicator. Definitions differ (forest land use vs tree cover); do not merge.

findings.claim: Q3: Projected changes in water availability by basin (Koshi, Gandaki, Karnali, Mahakali, and southern rivers): annual and dry-season flow, by scenario and horizon.
findings.period: projection horizons (e.g. 2021-2050, 2071-2100) vs stated baseline period
findings.note: Required: basin-level runoff projections (Khadka 2020 Koshi; Lutz 2014 upper Ganges; HI-WISE; Huss and Hock 2018 for glacier runoff). 25A owns cryosphere projection ranges PR-xx; 13B maps them to water availability and records only basin-level additions.

findings.claim: 13B does not duplicate 25A projection ranges; cryosphere_summary references 25A PR ids for glacier volume and peak-water, and 13B adds observed mass-balance and basin water-availability framing only.
Ecosystem losses are reported under welfare/environment objectives, not netted against GDP (consistent with 25E SIR-EC-1).
Glacier-runoff change and total-runoff change are different quantities; water availability uses total runoff with seasonal (dry-season) breakdown, and glacier-runoff only as a component.

data_gaps: No unit code for glacier mass balance (m w.e. per year) or area (km2) in src/economic_model/units.py.
No basin-specific runoff projection located for Gandaki, Karnali or Mahakali (only Koshi and upper Ganges aggregate).
FRTC, DNPWC, WDPA, FAO FRA, GFW and WECS URLs are from general knowledge and unverified.
No catalog id for UNEP-WCMC/WDPA, WRI/GFW, FRTC, DNPWC or WECS.
Biodiversity trend indicators (species status, Red List Index) not scoped with leads in r1.

assumptions.text: 25A projection ranges are referenced, not re-estimated.
Forest definitions (FAO/FRTC land use vs GFW tree-cover threshold) are kept as separate series and never spliced.
Ecosystem service changes enter welfare objectives, not GDP.

challenges.text: Add unit codes for glacier mass balance (m water-equivalent per year) and area (km2) to units.py, and catalog ids for WDPA, GFW, FRTC, DNPWC and WECS.
Please confirm PR ids 13B should reference for peak-water and dry-season flow so 13B water_availability_projections do not duplicate 25A ranges.
Hydropower planning should use basin dry-season availability ranges (when retrieved) rather than stationary historical flows; 13B will provide basin mapping.
Irrigation water availability in Terai depends on southern (non-snow-fed) rivers and groundwater, which glacier studies do not cover; request agriculture not infer from glacier projections.

uncertainty: High. Few in-situ benchmark glaciers represent Nepal's glacier population; geodetic and in-situ estimates differ in period and coverage; runoff projections vary by glacio-hydrological model, climate forcing and baseline period, with larger spread in precipitation than temperature; forest-cover trends depend strongly on definition and sensor.

cryosphere_summary.method: Table of observed mass-balance by glacier/region: source, method (glaciological/geodetic), period, value (m w.e./yr, unit code pending), uncertainty; plus inventory area change by basin; projections referenced from 25A PR ids.

tree-cover loss by year (GFW; separate definition)

ecosystem_baseline.method: Record each indicator with reference year, definition and source; trend computed only within a consistent definition.

water_availability_projections.method: By basin x scenario x horizon: change in annual and dry-season total runoff (percent vs stated baseline), glacier-melt share, peak-water timing referenced to 25A; observed baseline from DHM discharge.
